title: Read-populate races write-invalidate — cache-aside restores a stale value permanently
expected_feedback: Critical: classic cache-aside populate/invalidate interleaving. Order T1 (reader reads old from DB) → T2 (writer commits new to DB) → T3 (writer DELs the key) → T4 (reader SETs the value it read at T1). The DEL lands before the SET, so the reader resurrects the pre-write value. Because the SET uses expiration 0 the stale entry has no TTL, so it never self-heals — the cache serves a wrong balance until the next write to that account, which may never come. This is not fixed by reordering the writer (DB-then-DEL is already correct) because the reader's read-then-write window is what is unguarded. Fixes, in order of strength: (1) delayed double-delete — writer DELs, then DELs again after a delay exceeding the read window; (2) single-writer invalidation driven off the DB change log (CDC/binlog/outbox) so invalidation is not racing the application's own reads; (3) a per-key version/generation embedded in the cache key so a stale populate writes to a key nobody reads; (4) at minimum, a bounded jittered TTL so the staleness window is finite. Also discard-checked: both the SET and the DEL drop their errors, so a failed invalidation is invisible.
detector_note: The race is an ordering property across two functions — outside what a single-snippet regex can see. Gated compounding defects: unbounded TTL and discarded invalidation errors.
